extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers / creative writers working on character voice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating distinct, believable character voices in fiction, covering character understanding, use of description, avoiding clichés, and crafting dialogue that matches personality and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand your characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you can write distinct voices for your characters, it’s important to understand who they are; building out a solid foundation and developing compelling backstories ensures they always have unique voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write character sketches that detail backgrounds, personalities, goals, and motivations. Conduct interviews with your characters as if they were real people (the Proust questionnaire is suggested). Imagine how characters’ past experiences will change how they speak in different situations and emotional states. Ask about likes/dislikes, fears, and goals to inform speech patterns and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use description to enhance your characters’ voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions can be just as important as dialogue when creating character voices — body language, mannerisms, and behaviour contribute to how a character 'sounds' on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific details to create vivid descriptions of body language, mannerisms, and behaviour. Consider how mannerisms influence speech (e.g., a shy character may hesitate or repeat themselves). Pay attention to how characters interact with their environment (use hands, pacing, stillness). Use sensory details to create immersion (a nervous character might sweat or fidget with jewellery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotypes and clichés
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fall back on stereotypical or clichéd portrayals when creating voices; these produce one-dimensional characters and break authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using dialects or accents because they often rely on stereotypes and can break reader immersion unless authenticity is essential to the book. Consider how a character’s background and experiences influence beliefs and values rather than using stock archetypes. Think outside traditional archetypes and combine traits from multiple sources to create fresh, authentic voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft unique dialogue that reflects character
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert your understanding of characters into dialogue that feels authentic and unique to each character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read dialogue out loud to ensure it sounds true to the character. Give characters a natural conversational quirk (e.g., calling everyone 'love'). Vary sentence length and complexity to reflect personality and background. Consider education and experience when choosing vocabulary and sentence structure. Use dialogue tags sparingly so they don't detract from speech. Avoid excessive exposition in dialogue; let characters speak only when it serves the story.
